meta.description: Validate BAM integrity, reference-dictionary identity, alignment quality, contamination, and sample swaps with insert size, pairing, GC bias, strand balance, and post-alignment metrics. Use before variant calling or quantification.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All numeric claims cited in this report came from captured runs; no clinical outcomes or identifiers were fabricated.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill supplies research-data QC and explicitly leaves clinical interpretation to downstream research workflows.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill distinguishes generic DNA defaults from assay-specific expectations and documents the limits of slice-based contamination checks.

code_usability.detail: Both shipped validators parsed and ran across archived and fresh fixtures with documented 0/1/2 exit contracts.

functional_suitability.note: Covers integrity, dictionary identity, QC, contamination, sample swap, and assay-aware interpretation with runnable primary workflows.

reliability.note: Both validators have explicit success, QC-fail, and unreadable-input exit contracts, including missing @SQ and unresolved CRAM handling.

performance_context.note: The Python validator uses aggregate counters and an exact frequency median; a 5.642M-record run used 27,292 KB maximum RSS.

agent_usability.note: Decision-oriented sections, commands, thresholds, exits, and cross-skill boundaries are clear; the comprehensive reference remains necessarily long.

human_usability.note: The concise guide defers commands and thresholds to SKILL.md while retaining useful prompts and a quick-start path.

security.note: No credential, external-write, or unbounded destructive operation is instructed; inputs remain explicit local files.

maintainability.note: The two maintained examples share documented bands and contracts; detailed assay commands intentionally remain in their canonical related Skills.

agent_specific.note: Frontmatter now names integrity, dictionary, contamination, and swap triggers; the description and decision surface are specific without overpromising a real FREEMIX result.

inputs.label: Primary paired-end BAM validation
inputs.note: Both validators completed on the public human paired-end BAM; reported 99.96% mapping, expected insert statistics, and PASS verdicts.

assertions.text: Both shipped validators complete the canonical paired-end BAM workflow.
assertions.note: Archived regression output contains a contract-valid result for each validator.

assertions.text: The mapping rate is computed over primary records including unplaced unmapped reads.
assertions.note: The full-run output reports 5,640,000 mapped of 5,642,000 primary records in the stress confirmation.

assertions.text: The output gives an actionable verdict rather than only raw counts.
assertions.note: Both outputs end with the Quality Summary and a 0/1/2 contract.

assertions.text: The workflow remains within research QC scope.
assertions.note: It reports alignment quality only and does not diagnose an individual.

inputs.label: Archived defect-fixture regression set
inputs.note: Every one of the 58 archived BAM fixtures was rerun through both validators: 116 runs, valid 0/1/2 contract statuses, and no Python traceback.

assertions.text: All archived BAM fixtures are exercised by both validators.
assertions.note: archived-validator-regression.summary records 58 BAMs and 116 validator runs.

assertions.text: Each validator returns a documented contract status on every archived fixture.
assertions.note: No status outside 0, 1, or 2 was recorded.

assertions.text: Malformed inputs do not emit a Python traceback.
assertions.note: The regression harness explicitly checks stderr for Traceback and recorded none.

assertions.text: The regression set includes integrity, mapping, pairing, strand, and fingerprint fixtures.
assertions.note: The archived data tree contains planted defects, ladder cases, dictionary cases, and fingerprint inputs.

inputs.label: Fresh tiny, no-SQ, and unreadable-CRAM inputs
inputs.note: Fresh synthetic fixtures produced Python/shell exit pairs of 0/0 for 50 reads, 2/2 for no @SQ, and 2/2 for an unresolved CRAM.

assertions.text: A tiny valid BAM is not given a pairing or strand grade.
assertions.note: Both outputs say too few primary reads to grade pairing or strand balance.

assertions.text: A BAM without @SQ is rejected consistently.
assertions.note: Both validators return exit 2 on the fresh no-SQ fixture.

assertions.text: An unresolved CRAM is classified as unreadable rather than as a low-MAPQ QC failure.
assertions.note: Both validators return exit 2; shell stderr names REF_PATH or -T as the remedy.

assertions.text: Sampling behavior is disclosed to the user.
assertions.note: The Python validator prints the -n head-of-file bias warning.

inputs.label: Same-RG fingerprint collision
inputs.note: Synthetic mismatched BAMs sharing a read-group collision were compared by file and returned UNEXPECTED_MISMATCH with exit 1.

assertions.text: The documented CrosscheckFingerprints command groups by file.
assertions.note: The command contains CROSSCHECK_BY=FILE.

assertions.text: A same-RG/PU collision cannot collapse two input BAMs into one comparison group.
assertions.note: The output metric header reports CROSSCHECK_BY=FILE and separate file group values.

assertions.text: A mismatched same-SM pair produces a failing result.
assertions.note: crosscheck_by_file_rc=1 and the output contains UNEXPECTED_MISMATCH.

assertions.text: The workflow states a safe alternative for input metadata.
assertions.note: The Skill also instructs users to assign distinct RG IDs and PUs.

inputs.label: Picard chart and table contracts
inputs.note: Picard 3.5.0 wrote InsertSize and GC table outputs without charts, and wrote an InsertSize PDF when Rscript was available.

assertions.text: Insert-size metrics can be generated without the chart option.
assertions.note: insert-no-chart.txt exists and contains MEDIAN_INSERT_SIZE.

assertions.text: GC-bias metrics can be generated without the chart option.
assertions.note: Both GC detail and summary tables exist and include NORMALIZED_COVERAGE.

assertions.text: A chart run succeeds when Rscript is available.
assertions.note: insert_chart_rc=0 and insert-with-chart.pdf was asserted non-empty.

assertions.text: The Skill documents the optional R prerequisite precisely.
assertions.note: Version Compatibility and both Picard sections distinguish chart generation from table generation.

inputs.label: 5.642M-record full-file validation
inputs.note: A BAM assembled from 1,000 public BAM copies completed in 22.61 seconds at 27,292 KB maximum RSS with expected 99.96% mapping and 123/126/32 insert statistics.

assertions.text: The validator completes a multi-million-record full-file input.
assertions.note: The 5,642,000-primary-record run completed successfully.

assertions.text: The large-run mapping calculation is correct.
assertions.note: The output reports 5,640,000 mapped and 2,000 unmapped primary records.

assertions.text: The aggregate implementation avoids per-read MAPQ memory growth.
assertions.note: Maximum RSS was 27,292 KB while processing 5.642M primary records.

assertions.text: Insert summary statistics remain correct after the aggregation change.
assertions.note: Median 123, mean 126, and standard deviation 32 match the established public-fixture values.

inputs.label: Documentation and static contract review
inputs.note: The source changes were syntax-checked, source diff checked, and reviewed against the final-pass recommendation list.

assertions.text: The Python example parses after the aggregate-counter change.
assertions.note: py_compile completed successfully.

assertions.text: The shell example parses after the decoded-pass change.
assertions.note: bash -n completed successfully.

assertions.text: The guide uses the same strand quantity as the validator and Skill.
assertions.note: Its prompts and workflow now name forward fraction F/(F+R).

assertions.text: All nine prior open P2 recommendations have a corresponding source correction and evidence.
assertions.note: The final checkpoint and unique fix log enumerate each correction and its verification.

key_strengths: The two validators now agree on normal, tiny, missing-SQ, malformed, and unresolved-CRAM contracts.
The Skill explicitly separates integrity, dictionary identity, QC metrics, and fingerprinting rather than treating one tool as universal validation.
All archived fixtures and targeted fresh inputs have retained, runnable evidence.
The whole-file implementation now has measured bounded memory behavior at multi-million-record scale.
